A1.goal: Recognise a situation, changes in voice and a few basic instructions.

gist.title: What is the main man doing?
options: Asking guests for directions
Explaining rules to a group
Inviting everyone to dance
gist.why: He gives several instructions to other men.

gist.title: Does anybody speak while he is talking?
options: Yes; other men interrupt
No; the other men only listen
No; he speaks alone for the entire scene

detail.title: What special event is taking place?
options: A birthday dinner
A business meeting in the office
A wedding celebration
detail.why: He says it is his wedding day.

detail.title: Which activity does the speaker forbid?
options: Singing
Taking photographs
Racing
detail.why: He lists racing among the prohibited activities.

detail.title: Why does he want people to behave?
options: He does not want to embarrass someone
He wants to leave immediately
He worries about delays in the event programme
detail.why: He wants to prevent embarrassment at this important event.

sequence: He tells the men why today is special.
Someone asks a question about snow.
He says the most important rule again and again.

facts.title: Write the first name of the bride.

open.title: How does the main speaker feel? Write a short sentence.
open.answer: He sounds angry / stressed / worried about the event.
open.criteria: Accept a clear adjective with a simple reason based on voice or situation.

A2.goal: Understand the purpose of the exchange and selected concrete details.

gist.title: What does the speaker mainly want to achieve?
options: Arrange transport for all the visitors
Prevent trouble during an event
Keep the guests entertained
gist.why: His instructions are meant to prevent trouble.

gist.title: How do the other men respond?
options: They all agree loudly with him
They laugh at him and walk away
Some question or interrupt him
gist.why: Several men interrupt or challenge him.

detail.title: What occasion does the speaker refer to?
options: His own wedding
A family funeral
A military ceremony
detail.why: He explicitly identifies the occasion as his wedding day.

detail.title: Which of these is on his forbidden-activities list?
options: Opening presents
Playing board games
Telling fortunes
detail.why: Fortune-telling is one of the activities he rejects.

detail.title: What does he do with his final instruction?
options: He repeats it forcefully
He whispers it once
He writes it down on a piece of paper
detail.why: Repetition and raised volume intensify his final warning.

sequence: He tells the men what day it is.
A man says the speaker broke a promise.
He talks about the other family.

facts.title: Which woman's name does the speaker say? Write her first name.

open.title: Explain ONE reason why the scene becomes tense.
open.answer: The groups dislike each other (bad blood); some guests are in uniform; the speaker fears trouble.
open.criteria: Accept any grounded cause, in one or two clear sentences.

B1.goal: Follow the key conflict, specific restrictions and changes in tone.

gist.title: Which summary best matches the scene?
options: A host tries to control a risky social gathering
Two friends plan a surprise celebration
An embarrassed guest apologises for a serious misunderstanding
gist.why: The speaker attempts to prevent conflict at an important event.

gist.title: What creates some of the humour?
options: The speaker tells a long joke about the wedding
The men keep laughing at the clothes the speaker is wearing
Unexpected interruptions in the middle of serious warnings
gist.why: The interruptions contrast with the speaker’s determination.

detail.title: One man says the speaker broke a promise. What was the promise?
options: There would be no relatives at the party
There would be no uniforms
There would be more musicians at the event
detail.why: A man complains about the presence of uniforms.

detail.title: Which unusual thing does the speaker forbid?
options: Leaving a coat in the kitchen
Taking fuel from other people’s cars
Using a telephone during the ceremony
detail.why: He forbids siphoning petrol from the guests’ cars.

detail.title: What happens to the final warning?
options: He says it only once, and very quietly
He makes a joke about it
He repeats it, louder each time
detail.why: His final command grows louder through repetition.

sequence: He tells the men what day it is.
A man complains about something the speaker had promised.
He talks about the bride's family.
Someone asks a question that seems off-topic.

open.title: Why does one man complain at the start, and how does the speaker deal with it?
open.answer: He complains that there are uniforms although the speaker promised there would be none; the speaker just says "Nevertheless" and carries on.
open.criteria: Mention the broken promise (uniforms) and the speaker's dismissive reply.

B2.goal: Understand what is meant but not said, idioms, and how the characters relate to each other.

gist.title: What is the speaker trying to do?
options: To announce a business deal for the future
To make sure the day goes without trouble
To make the two families friends for good
gist.why: His aim is to prevent trouble during the gathering.

gist.title: Why are the men's interruptions important?
options: They make it harder for him to keep control
They show that the men support the bride's family
They make fun of him in front of the guests
gist.why: Their objections and off-topic questions make control difficult.

detail.title: One man complains about the uniforms. Why does this matter?
options: It reminds everyone that the two groups do not get on
It shows that the men would like to join the army themselves
It suggests that the wedding may be cancelled
detail.why: The uniforms remind everyone of the bad blood between the groups.

detail.title: One man says he was only trying to "sell" the speaker. What does he mean?
options: He was trying to make him look good
He was warning everyone about the speaker's debts
He was offering the speaker a business deal
detail.why: "Sell" here means to talk him up and make him look good.

detail.title: He repeats his last order several times. What is the effect?
options: It shows that the problem is already solved
It shows that he has given up trying to control them
It makes the order stronger and more forceful
detail.why: Repetition and shouting turn an instruction into an emphatic threat.

sequence: He reminds the men what day it is.
One of the men protests about the guests' clothing.
He explains why nothing must go wrong today.
Someone asks about snow.

facts.title: What word does he use for the group in uniform?

open.title: Does the way he speaks help him get what he wants? Give examples from the scene.
open.answer: He seeks peace and restraint while using anger, intimidation and forceful threats.
open.criteria: Identify both the de-escalatory aim and the aggressive delivery; support both with evidence.

C1.goal: Interpret indirect meanings, interpersonal power, idiomatic speech and comic incongruity.

gist.title: Which tension is most central to the scene?
options: An explicit rejection of family ties in favour of individual freedom
An effort to obtain approval through careful politeness
An attempt to create order performed through verbal aggression
gist.why: He demands restraint while speaking aggressively.

gist.title: What best explains the scene’s mixture of danger and comedy?
options: Severe warnings collide with trivial or inappropriate concerns
The speaker deliberately jokes to make his rules easier to accept
The men openly laugh at the speaker's anger
gist.why: The incongruity of threats and mundane requests creates dark humour.

detail.title: What is the rhetorical force of “nevertheless” after an objection?
options: He admits the objection is valid and promises to fix the problem
He rejects the objection as a lie
He acknowledges the objection but overrides it
detail.why: He acknowledges a challenge only to override it.

detail.title: Why is “spinning yarns” not meant literally here?
options: The man is accused of telling dubious stories about him
The man is accused of wasting everyone's time with pointless small talk
The man is accused of revealing family secrets
detail.why: The idiom refers to exaggerating or inventing stories.

detail.title: How would you best describe the register?
options: Colloquial and profane, but mostly polite requests
Colloquial, profane and imperative
Formal and ceremonious, apart from a few swear words

sequence: He invokes the significance of the day.
A listener disputes what had been agreed.
He turns to the bride and her family.
A question about "snow" interrupts him.

facts.title: Which woman is explicitly at the centre of the speaker’s concern? Give her first name.

open.title: Analyse one interruption: what does it do to the speaker's control of the conversation?
open.answer: A mundane or inappropriate question diverts attention from his severe warning and forces a shift in topic.
open.criteria: Name an observable interruption and show how it alters conversational power or pacing.

C2.goal: Critically analyse power, register and comic timing in authentic colloquial dialogue.

gist.title: Which reading best captures the scene’s paradox?
options: The speaker demands restraint while admitting that he himself provoked the conflict
The speaker demands restraint but secretly hopes for a fight
The speaker demands restraint while modelling rhetorical escalation
gist.why: His attempt to stop conflict is itself verbally aggressive.

gist.title: What is a plausible counter-reading of the speaker’s shouting?
options: It shows he has already lost the men's respect
It is mainly meant to be heard by the guests outside the room
It could reveal concern that his authority may be fragile
gist.why: His volume can signify both attempted dominance and threatened composure.

detail.title: How does the concessive marker after the objection operate?
options: It acknowledges resistance while retaining the floor
It concedes the point and promises a compromise later
It signals sarcastic agreement with the objection
detail.why: He briefly registers the challenge without relinquishing control.

detail.title: What does the appeal to a shared external antagonist accomplish?
options: It defines a perceived outside provocation to be resisted
It shifts responsibility away from any of the men present
It reveals that no actual disagreement exists
detail.why: He places group restraint in the context of hostility from outsiders.

detail.title: Which conclusion about power is best supported by the clip alone?
options: Authority is loudly asserted but repeatedly negotiated in talk
The speaker's authority collapses completely and visibly by the end of the scene
The interruptions show the men openly reject his authority
detail.why: We observe claims to authority and interruptions, not later compliance or mental states.

sequence: He invokes the day itself as grounds for compliance.
Prior terms are contested.
He turns to the bride and her family.
An off-topic question about "snow" intervenes.

facts.title: Which woman does the speaker name? Give her first name.

open.title: Evaluate the speaker's strategy for keeping order: how far does it persuade, and how far does it coerce?
open.answer: His justification concerns another person’s welfare, yet his threats and profanity rely on intimidation; a counter-reading may emphasise a volatile setting.
open.criteria: Make a nuanced argument with one supporting detail and an explicit counter-reading.
